case_name: Haryana State Cooperative Labour and others v Unique Cooperative Labour and others
petitioner: Haryana State Cooperative Labour and others
facts: The Haryana State Cooperative Labour and Construction Federation Ltd. (Haryana Federation) was engaged in the execution of Government works.
In 1981, the Haryana Federation was assigned the work of construction of low income group houses in Sector 15, Panchkula, Haryana, by the Haryana Housing Board.
The Haryana Federation entered into three separate construction contracts with respondent no. 1 - Unique Cooperative Labour and Construction Cooperative Society Ltd.
The Haryana Federation referred three disputes against the work awarding agency - the Haryana Housing Board, to the Registrar, Cooperative Societies, Haryana.
An Arbitrator was appointed to adjudicate upon all the three disputes, and passed three different awards on 28.12.1987.
The payment received by the Haryana Federation was transmitted by it to the Construction Society.
The Construction Society raised a separate dispute in connection with the contractual agreement dated 20.7.1981.
Arbitration proceedings commenced on 2.11.2007, and culminated in an award dated 20.2.2008.

The Haryana Federation assailed the award dated 20.2.2008 before various authorities, including the Registrar, Cooperative Societies, Haryana, the Principal Secretary, Department of Cooperation, Government of Haryana, the High Court, and the Letters Patent Bench.
issues: Whether the Haryana Federation was entitled to assail the arbitral award dated 20.2.2008 under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
Whether the delay in filing objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act was justified.
petitioner_arguments: The Haryana Federation argued that it had a right to assail the arbitral award dated 20.2.2008 under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
The Haryana Federation contended that the delay in filing objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act was justified due to various reasons.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the Haryana Federation had waived its right to assail the arbitral award dated 20.2.2008 by not doing so earlier.
The respondent contended that the delay in filing objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act was unexplained and unjustified.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the Haryana Federation had a right to assail the arbitral award dated 20.2.2008 under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
The Court found that the delay in filing objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act was not justified and was contrary to the provisions of the Arbitration Act.
holding: The Court dismissed the Haryana Federation's objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act, holding that the delay in filing the same was unexplained and unjustified.
